mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 3% in the month preceding the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean of the prior 30 months (p > 0.1) during FEDFUNDS > 3.0% periods.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) while UNRATE remains below 5.5% signals labor market strength that precedes a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: Over a 5-year window, 60-day forward returns are not positively correlated with PAYEMS above median UNRATE (Pearson IC < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both HOUST (residential construction) and INDPRO (industrial production) for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak demand suppresses corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < INDPRO previous month AND HOUST < INDPRO current month
failure_condition: During such dual-month declines, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 12-month mean (p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 5% from the prior quarter is followed by a negative S&P 5-day forward return as weak supply signals near-term profit compression.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.15) during such INDPRO drops.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-month decline in GDPC1 (GDP) accompanied by a parallel rise in FEDFUNDS predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as economic expansion weakens and rates stay elevated.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous quarter AND FEDFUNDS rising
regime_hint: weakening growth with persistent rate hikes
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negatively correlated with the composite signal (Pearson IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 60-day forward return tends to be positive due to expectations of lower wage growth and reduced inflationary pressure.
failure_condition: Over 10 such regimes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the baseline (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in RSAFS (available for sale) exceeding 10% of the prior month's value while HOUST remains flat suggests excess liquidity, which precedes a positive S&P 20-day return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day rolling mean during such spikes (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in CPIAUCSL (CPI) by over 2% in the prior month while INDPRO remains above 110 (2017=100) indicates a supply-side shock that precedes a negative S&P 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.2) during such events.
